data.narrative:
Quantum Machines is a Series C quantum computing company that has raised $280M to date. The quantum computing sector comprises 11 comparable entities—3 public (IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, PsiQuantum, and SandboxAQ—though the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables for reliable median benchmarking.

Stage-progression analysis, the sole applicable triangulation method, applies a typical Series C-to-next-stage multiplier of 1.7x to the $280M raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $476M. This method captures expected expansion in scale and capital efficiency typical of frontier-tech companies advancing through institutional fundraising stages. Peer-median analysis was not feasible; while 8 quantum computing private companies exist as reference points, none meet the minimum three-datapoint threshold when filtered by stage and valuation tier, making sector-wide median comparison unreliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $405M to $547M, centered on $476M. Key uncertainties include the absence of same-stage or similarly-valued private comparables to validate the step-up assumption and limited public trading history in quantum computing to ground sector-wide multiples. The range reflects ±15% confidence bounds around the stage-progression estimate rather than independent methodological confirmation.
